title: hivemind_find returns 0 results for every query despite 13 stored memories with embeddings
description:
hivemind_stats reports: memories 13, embeddings 13, healthy true, ollama_available true, all 13 chunks under collection "opencode-swarm". So storage is working.

But hivemind_find returns {"results": [], "count": 0} for EVERY query tried, including single-word queries that must match stored content: "moonrepo", "kata", "template", and "moon template tera interpolation kata bun". Workers in this epic explicitly stored moon/Tera/template learnings that these queries should hit.

Impact: this is severe and silent. Every swarm worker prompt mandates "query hivemind BEFORE writing any code". Workers run the query, get 0 results, correctly conclude "no prior art", and proceed — so the failure looks identical to a genuinely greenfield repo. The swarm's collective memory is write-only: it accumulates learnings that can never be retrieved, and every agent repeats work the previous one already did.

Timeline note: at the start of this epic Ollama was down and hivemind_store failed outright (a researcher reported two failed attempts). Ollama is up now and stores succeed. So embedding generation recovered, but retrieval did not — suggesting the issue is in the query/similarity path rather than the embedding path. Possible leads: memories written while Ollama was down may have null/zero-vector embeddings inflating the count; or a similarity threshold that filters everything; or a collection-scoping mismatch (all chunks are under "opencode-swarm" while find may default to "default").

Repro: hivemind_stats (shows 13/13 healthy) then hivemind_find(query="kata", limit=10) -> 0 results.
